title: Belgium – Telephone and data transmission services – Inventorisation et nettoyage bacs de liaison réseau fibre optique
description: L’objet du marché est la conclusion d’accords-cadres pour l’inventorisation et le nettoyage des chambres de visite du réseau de fibres optiques de Sibelga. Par inventorisation, on entend la cartographie systématique et la documentation de toutes les données pertinentes, telles que la localisation précise, les caractéristiques physiques, la structure interne et l’état technique des chambres de visite, ainsi que l’infrastructure de câbles présente, comme les conduites, les câbles et les sous-conduits. Les facteurs environnementaux susceptibles d’avoir un impact sur la gestion, l’entretien ou les travaux futurs sont également pris en compte. Le but du marché est de conclure un Accord-Cadre en cascade avec les 2 premiers Soumissionnaires classés suivant les critères d’attribution. Seul le Soumissionnaire classé premier suivant les critères d’attribution sera considéré comme Adjudicataire « actif ». L’autre Soumissionnaire, (classé deuxième), sera considéré comme Adjudicataire « de réserve ». Son contrat pourra être activé qu’en cas de défaillance de l’Adjudicataire actif.

title: Romania – Technical analysis or consultancy services – Servicii de consultanță în management pentru proiectul “Consolidare și reabilitare Palat Administrativ – Corp A”
description: Prin achiziția serviciilor de consultanță specializată pentru managementul proiectului se va asigura cadrul necesar implementării eficiente a proiectului „Consolidare și reabilitare Palat Administrativ – Corp A”, cu respectarea obligațiilor asumate prin contractul de finanțare, a cerințelor finanțatorului și a legislației aplicabile. Serviciile de consultanță vor avea ca scop sprijinirea beneficiarului în coordonarea generală a proiectului, monitorizarea progresului fizic și financiar, urmărirea respectării termenelor asumate, gestionarea documentelor aferente implementării, sprijinirea procesului de achiziții, monitorizarea contractelor, verificarea încadrării cheltuielilor în bugetul aprobat, precum și elaborarea documentațiilor și rapoartelor solicitate de finanțator. Implementarea corespunzătoare a proiectului presupune o monitorizare permanentă a gradului de realizare a activităților, a indicatorilor asumați și a rezultatelor propuse, precum și identificarea și gestionarea eventualelor riscuri care pot apărea pe parcursul derulării proiectului. În acest context, experiența și competențele unui operator economic specializat în managementul proiectelor cu finanțare nerambursabilă reprezintă un element important pentru asigurarea unei implementări eficiente și conforme. Astfel, pentru realizarea acestui obiectiv, ofertantul declarat câştigător al procedurii de atribuire va asigura cel puțin următoarele categorii de servicii: - Asistență și suport pentru monitorizarea contractului de finanțare și a documentelor anexate, pentru respectarea termenelor și condițiilor asumate; - Asistență în monitorizarea contractelor de achiziție publică încheiate în cadrul proiectului; - Gestionarea platformei MySMIS2021 dedicată implementării proiectului; - Asistență în realizarea și monitorizarea cash-flow-ului pe întreaga perioadă de implementare a proiectului; - Elaborarea și documentarea cererilor de prefinanțare/plată/rambursare; - Asistență în relația dintre autoritatea contractantă și AGENȚIA PENTRU DEZVOLTARE REGIONALĂ A REGIUNII DE DEZVOLTARE SUD – EST (ADR SE), în calitate de Autoritate de management pentru Programul Regional Sud-Est 2021-2027, pe parcursul implementării proiectului; - asistență în monitorizarea respectării regulilor privind vizibilitatea Uniunii Europene, în conformitate cu manualul de identitate vizuală aplicabil Programului Regional Sud-Est 2021-2027; - elaborarea rapoartelor de activitate, precum și a celor stabilite prin cererea și contractul de finanțare. Detalii suplimentare se regăsesc în Caietul de sarcini. Numarul de zile pana la care se pot solicita clarificari inainte de data limita de depunere a ofertelor este de 20 zile. Autoritatea Contractanta va raspunde o singura data solicitarilor de clarificari in a 11-a zi inainte de data limita de depunere a ofertelor.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Metrohm - i-Raman NXG 785 S system
description: This request is for the purchase of a Metrohm i-Raman NXG 785 S system which is a commercial off the shelf (COTS), portable Raman instrument. This acquisition replaces an obsolete, unrepairable Raman spectrometer (from B&W Tek, now owned by Metrohm) to prevent loss of critical analytical capability supporting NMAM method publication and implementation. Modern Raman technology improves sensitivity, reliability, and serviceability while maintaining portability for field-relevant applications. Additionally, this request is for the purchase of one ?Stat-i M8ONE (Bi)potentiostat/Galvanostat/Impedance Analyzer (EIS). This instrument will support CBMB researchers in ongoing dermal penetration studies using Franz cells by measuring impedance across skin membranes and generating high-quality graphs for publications and presentations. It will replace a single-channel unit and enable researchers to perform up to 16 simultaneous experiments instead of one at a time, significantly reducing experiment time and accelerating the delivery of results. Additional cables and training are provided as part of the package. The vendor will install the instrument, ensure correct operation, and train operators onsite for one day (i-Raman NXG) and 4 hours and online (?Stat-i M8ONE EIS) as needed. An existing CDC laboratory desktop connected to the ISLE (CDC Property # 357548) will be used to operate the i-Raman NXG 785 S instrument using the SpecSuite software. The NIOSH request for level III approval for the SpecSuite software has been submitted. The ?Stat-i M8ONE EIS instrument runs on DropView software which the laboratory possesses currently, but may require an upgrade. It will not require any additional external computer system for operation. The instrument is designated for laboratory use only and will be connected to the current ISLE system.

title: FCI Three Rivers - Cooling-Tower and Closed-Loop Water Treatment Services
description: TITLE: Sources Sought � Cooling-Tower and Closed-Loop Water Treatment Services � FCI Three Rivers NOTICE TYPE: Sources Sought NAICS CODE: 325998 � All Other Miscellaneous Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD: 650 employees DESCRIPTION: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Three Rivers, is conducting market research in accordance with RFO Part 10 for an anticipated requirement for cooling-tower and closed-loop water-treatment services. This notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for quotation, or request for proposal. The Government will not award a contract based on this notice and will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing a response. A response to this notice is not required to participate in any future solicitation. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Federal Correctional Institution Three Rivers 1700 Highway 72 West Three Rivers, Texas 78071 PRELIMINARY REQUIREMENT: The anticipated requirement includes comprehensive water-treatment services for the institution�s cooling-tower condenser and closed-loop water systems. The preliminary scope includes: Chemical treatment of Evapco cooling-tower condenser systems supporting approximately 1,905 tons of air-conditioning capacity. Treatment intended to control scale, corrosion, fouling, and biological growth. Twice-monthly servicing of the cooling-tower treatment program. Monthly servicing of chilled-water, hot-water, and combined chilled/hot-water closed-loop systems. Testing of closed-loop systems for proper inhibitor levels. Filter changes and addition of chemical inhibitors as required. Furnishing all required treatment chemicals, chemical feeders, filters, equipment, testing materials, and related supplies. Sampling and laboratory analysis. Annual inspections and specified chemical cleanings. Written service reports, test results, chemical-use information, trend analysis, and corrective recommendations. Routine service-call response within 24 hours of notification. On-site response within eight hours for a critical life-safety emergency. The Government anticipates a firm-fixed-price service contract consisting of a base year and four one-year option periods. The final contract structure, service frequencies, response times, pricing units, and performance requirements will be developed after consideration of industry feedback. The work will be performed at a secure Federal correctional institution. Prior correctional-facility experience is not required. Contractor personnel requiring institutional access will be subject to applicable security, screening, escort, and access procedures. INFORMATION REQUESTED: Interested businesses should complete the attached Market Research Questionnaire and provide the following information: Legal business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Unique Entity Identifier and CAGE Code. Current SAM.gov registration status and expiration date. Business size and applicable socioeconomic categories under NAICS 325998. Whether the firm can perform the complete requirement as the prime contractor. Any anticipated subcontracting or teaming arrangement, including the work each party would perform. Geographic service location and routine service radius for supporting FCI Three Rivers. Relevant experience providing similar cooling-tower and closed-loop water-treatment services. Technical qualifications, licenses, certifications, and laboratory accreditations. Ability to furnish the required chemicals, filters, chemical feeders, equipment, sampling, testing, and reporting. Ability to meet the proposed 24-hour routine service-call response and eight-hour critical-emergency response. Customary commercial pricing units and contract practices for these services. Do not submit a price quote. Identification of any Government contract vehicle covering these services, including GSA Multiple Award Schedule SIN 325998W, if applicable. Questions, concerns, or recommended revisions concerning the attached draft Statement of Work. Recommendations concerning measurable treatment outcomes, target ranges, sampling points, testing methods, reporting metrics, service frequencies, and customary emergency-response standards. RESPONSE FORMAT: Respondents should submit the completed Market Research Questionnaire. Firms may also submit a capability statement not exceeding three additional pages. Copies of licenses, certifications, and laboratory accreditations will not count toward the three-page limitation. Clearly identify and mark any proprietary or confidential information. Do not submit a quotation, proposal, or detailed pricing. Responses may be submitted through SAM.gov or by email to: Brandy Perez Contract Specialist Email: b5Perez@bop.gov Responses must be received no later than September 10, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. Central Time. Suggested email subject line: Sources Sought Response � FCI Three Rivers Cooling-Tower Water Treatment Services INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT: The Government may conduct a voluntary site visit or one-on-one industry discussions to obtain additional information and refine the requirement. Participation in any industry engagement will be voluntary and will not affect eligibility to compete for a future contract. DISCLAIMER: The Government will use the information received to evaluate industry capability, small-business participation, potential contract vehicles, customary commercial practices, and the appropriate acquisition strategy. No solicitation is currently available. If a solicitation is issued, it will be announced separately through the appropriate Government system. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or make an award as a result of this notice.

title: Repair Academy Fences
description: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, and supervision necessary to service, repair, reset, and replace damaged or deficient fence components at the United States Coast Guard Academy, 15 Mohegan Drive, New London, Connecticut. Work includes replacing only fence posts that are loose, damaged, rotted, bent, broken, or otherwise unable to support the fence; resetting designated posts; replacing damaged chain link, top rail, bottom rail, bracing, tension wire, barbed wire, hardware, caps, bands, ties, clamps, and related components; excavating failed concrete footings; installing new galvanized posts set in concrete; restoring disturbed areas; and ensuring all repaired fence sections are plumb, aligned, stable, properly tensioned, and fully functional. Work areas include the tennis courts, perimeter fence, U-Lot, and track fence, with all work to be coordinated with the Technical Advisor and performed in a manner that minimizes disruption to Coast Guard Academy operations.

title: Parking lot construction - Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site
description: 5P468-26-0166/A Parking lot construction - Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca . Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other thansoumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada requires contractor to supply and operation of machinery and operators for the construction of a new 700’ x 130’ gravel parking lot on the Fortress of Louisbourg National Historic Site location. See Statement of Work for further details on the requirement of this project. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $100,001 > $ 250,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI03 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work from October 1, 2026 to December 15, 2026. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT It is recommended that the Bidder or a representative of the Bidder visit the work site. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at Gate 1 on route 22 at Louisbourg, NS. 295 Park Service Road B1C 2L2 on September 4, 11:00 am. Bidders must communicate with the Contracting Authority 24h before the optional site visit to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Finland – Health and social work services – Tuetun asumisen palvelut
description: Tuomi Logistiikka Oy pyytää Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueen toimeksiannosta tarjouksia tuetun asumisen palvelun hankinnasta. Tuettu asuminen on sosiaalihuoltolain (1301/2014) 21a§:n mukaista yksilökohtaista sosiaaliohjauksellista tukea henkilölle, joka erityisestä syystä tarvitsee hyvinvointialueen apua tai tukea itsenäiseen asumiseen tai siihen siirtymiseen. Tuetun asumisen palvelu on suunnattu täysi-ikäisille Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueen järjestämisvelvollisuuden piiriin kuuluville asiakkaille. Tuetun asumisen palvelua voidaan myöntää henkilölle, joka erityisestä syystä tarvitsee apua tai tukea itsenäisessä asumisessa ja/tai itsenäisen asumisensa järjestämisessä. Tuki kohdistuu itsenäisen elämän mahdollistamiseen, osallistumisen vahvistamiseen ja turvalliseen arkeen, jossa asiakkaan omat valinnat ja itsemääräämisoikeus toteutuvat. Tuetun asumisen palvelu toteutetaan asiakkaan omassa kodissa tai Palveluntuottajan vuokraamassa asunnossa. Hankittava palvelu koostuu seuraavista tukijaksoista: - Tukijakso 1A: ohjaus- ja tukityöskentely enintään 60 tuntia enintään 6 kuukauden aikajaksolla. - Tukijakso 1B: ohjaus- ja tukityöskentely enintään 6 tuntia kuukaudessa enintään 12 kuukauden ajan. - Tukijakso 1C: ohjaus- ja tukityöskentely yksilöllisen päätöksen mukaisesti (noin 10-12 tuntia kuukaudessa). Hankinta on jaettu maantieteellisesti osa-alueisiin seuraavasti: 1. Tampere, Pirkkala 2. Kangasala, Orivesi, Kuhmoinen, Pälkäne 3. Ylöjärvi, Ikaalinen, Hämeenkyrö 4. Nokia, Sastamala, Punkalaidun 5. Lempäälä, Vesilahti, Valkeakoski, Akaa, Urjala 6. Virrat, Ruovesi, Parkano, Kihniö 7. Optio: Mänttä-Vilppula, Juupajoki Sopimuskausi alkaa 1.1.2027 ja on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvioitu arvo on noin 6 miljoonaa euroa vuodessa. Laskennallinen neljän vuoden hankinnan arvo on tällöin arviolta 24 milj. euroa. Hankintasopimuksen perusteella tehtävien tilausten määrät vaihtelevat tilaajan tarpeen mukaan, eikä hankintasopimus sisällä määrä- tai vähimmäisostovelvoitetta. Hankinnan kohde ja vähimmäisvaatimukset on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.

title: FCI Three Rivers - Wastewater Sampling and Laboratory Analysis Services
description: SOURCES SOUGHT / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT SAMPLING AND LABORATORY ANALYSIS SERVICES FEDERAL CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTION THREE RIVERS The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution (FCI) Three Rivers, is conducting market research in accordance with RFO Part 10 for an anticipated requirement for wastewater sample collection, transportation, accredited laboratory analysis, and regulatory compliance-reporting support. This notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, Request for Quotation, or Request for Proposal. The Government will not award a contract based on this notice and will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. A response to this notice is not required to participate in any future solicitation. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Federal Correctional Institution Three Rivers 1700 Highway 72 West Three Rivers, Texas 78071 PRELIMINARY REQUIREMENT The anticipated services will support compliance with the FCI Three Rivers Wastewater Treatment Facility�s Texas Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permit No. WQ0013461001, EPA ID No. TX0130052, including any renewal, replacement, or amendment in effect during contract performance. Current permit-monitoring requirements include: Weekly grab-sample monitoring for carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand, five-day; total suspended solids; ammonia nitrogen; and dissolved oxygen. Monthly grab-sample monitoring for E. coli and pH. Monitoring of flow and chlorine residual five times per week. Potential annual soil sampling and analysis when treated effluent is applied through irrigation. Anticipated contractor responsibilities may include: Furnishing appropriate sample containers, preservatives, labels, and related supplies. Collecting representative samples from Government-designated permitted monitoring locations. Preparing and maintaining complete chain-of-custody documentation. Providing temperature-controlled transportation and courier services. Meeting applicable sample-preservation and holding-time requirements. Performing analyses through appropriately accredited laboratories. Conducting quality-control review of analytical results. Providing electronic analytical reports and Discharge Monitoring Report-ready result summaries. Promptly notifying the Government of results that may exceed permit limits or otherwise require immediate attention. Correcting, recollecting, or reanalyzing rejected or compromised samples, as applicable. Potentially performing annual soil sampling and analysis associated with treated-effluent irrigation. The final Statement of Work will establish the division of responsibilities between institution personnel and the contractor for flow, chlorine residual, dissolved oxygen, pH, sample collection, off-site laboratory analysis, soil monitoring, reporting, and related activities. The Government is seeking industry recommendations concerning customary commercial practices, sampling schedules, courier limitations, analytical turnaround times, critical-result notifications, contract structure, performance standards, and appropriate pricing units. NAICS AND BUSINESS SIZE The anticipated North American Industry Classification System code is 541380, Testing Laboratories and Services. The applicable small-business size standard is $19 million in average annual receipts. The results of this market research may be used to determine whether the anticipated acquisition should be conducted as a small-business set-aside, under a specific socioeconomic program, through an existing Government contract vehicle, or through another appropriate acquisition strategy. RESPONSE REQUIREMENTS Interested businesses shall provide the following: A completed copy of the attached FCI Three Rivers Wastewater Sampling and Laboratory Analysis Market Research Questionnaire. If needed, a capability statement of no more than three additional pages addressing the company�s ability to perform the anticipated requirement. The company�s legal business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, email address, Unique Entity Identifier, CAGE Code, and SAM.gov registration status. The company�s business size and applicable socioeconomic categories under NAICS 541380. Identification of the proposed laboratory and courier locations that would support FCI Three Rivers, including the estimated courier time from the institution. Identification of applicable laboratory accreditations, fields of accreditation, analytical methods, quality-system certifications, and personnel qualifications. An explanation of whether the company can provide the complete requirement as the prime contractor or whether subcontractors or teaming partners would be used. Identification of the services and analyses that would be performed by subcontractors, including the proposed subcontracted laboratory�s name, location, accreditation, business size, and anticipated role. Two examples of recent and relevant experience performing wastewater compliance sampling and laboratory analysis under a TPDES, NPDES, or comparable permit. Recommendations concerning the division of responsibilities, turnaround times, critical-result notification requirements, electronic reporting formats, sampling schedules, courier restrictions, and customary pricing units. The number of calendar days the company would require following award to begin complete performance. Whether the company would participate in a voluntary site walkthrough, one-on-one industry engagement session, or both. Copies of licenses, certifications, laboratory accreditations, and current fields of accreditation will not count against the three-page capability-statement limit. Respondents shall clearly identify any proprietary or confidential information. Do not submit a price quotation or proposal in response to this notice. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Responses must be received no later than September 10, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. Central Time. Responses shall be submitted by email to: Brandy Perez Contract Specialist Federal Correctional Institution Three Rivers Email: b5Perez@bop.gov The email subject line should state: SOURCES SOUGHT RESPONSE � FCI THREE RIVERS WASTEWATER LABORATORY SERVICES Registration on the SAM.gov Interested Vendors List alone will not constitute a response. title: NATO Business Opportunity: Force Lethality Enhancement eXtended (FLEX) Modelling and Simulation Study
description: Headquarters, Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) is initiating Force Lethality Enhancement eXtended (FLE(X)), building upon the outcomes of the initial FLE study conducted in 2025. FLE focused on identifying novel options to deliver NATO Defense Planning Process (NDPP) Capability Targets (CT) in whole or in part. FLE(X) broadens the scope to include exploratory questions that look at the evolving operational problem sets that drive requirements and then CT. FLE(X) aims to identify new ways and means of achieving operational effects and to accelerate the translation of innovation into operational capabilities. FLE(X) will explore how the rapid adoption of new and emerging technologies, including robotics, autonomy, artificial intelligence, advanced networking, and precision-strike systems, can enhance the lethality of the NATO force and improve survivability, agility, sustainability and affordability. The studies will seek to deliver evidence-based insights that can support national decision-making on capability options and inform future NATO capability development including force-design activities. The contractor will provide analytical support through mission analysis, modelling and simulation, and structured evaluation of operationally relevant use-cases to identify credible opportunities for enhancement. This work will form part of a broader evidence base developed by ACT and participating Allies to inform the transformation of the Alliance�s military instrument. In lieu of a bidder�s conference, HQ SACT invites bidders to submit technical and contractual questions not later than 21 August 2026. Bids shall be received at HQ SACT, Purchasing and Contracting Office, no later than 10 September 2026, 9:00 am. No bids shall be accepted after this date and time. No hard copy proposals will be accepted. Please see RFP for submission instructions. REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL Please see attached. BIDDING PROCEDURE A Declaration of Eligibility is NOT required for this opportunity. Do NOT submit your proposal to the Department of Commerce. title: Rental of Secure Storage Facility for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE. THIS IS A NOTICE OF THE GOVERNMENT�S INTENT TO ISSUE A SOLE SOURCE AWARD TO TOWN OF LANCASTER (NY) FOR THE RENTAL OF A SECURE STORAGE FACILITY. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Office of Acquisition Management (OAQ), on behalf of the Enforcement & Removal Operations (ERO), intends to award a firm-fixed price purchase order on a sole source basis to Town of Lancaster, NY (SAM UEI Number W3HVB3149KQ9, CAGE Code 4SC34) (Address: Town of Lancaster, 21 Central Avenue, Suite 5, Lancaster, NY 14086-2128) for the rental of its secure security storage facility operated by the Lancaster Police Department (LPD), located at 525 Pavement Road, Lancaster , NY. The LPD secure storage facility is located in a secure location, on property owned by the Town of Lancaster. The facility is located behind a fence that encompasses the property, and there is on-duty law enforcement (LPD) stationed on-site. As such, the property on which the LPD secure storage facility is located provides a secure environment in which to store assets required by the ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office in support of mission requirements of its Special Response Team (SRT). Storing these agency assets at any other secure storage facility in the Buffalo, NY metro area would present a significant logistical challenge with respect to the coordination of the pick-up/drop-off of assets at the two ICE/ERO facilities (Buffalo Field Office in downtown Buffalo and the Buffalo Federal Detention Facility (BFDF) in Batavia, NY) located within the ICE/ERO Buffalo Area of Responsibility (AoR) . It is therefore necessary to continue to utilize the LPD secure facility to store all SRT assets in a central location between the ICE/ERO Buffalo and Batavia facilities. The LPD facility is within close proximity (five miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport. Proximity to the airport is required because of the many times SRT is deployed to assist ERO flights at the airport. Based upon the Market Research conducted by ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office, and a consideration of available commercial sources and law enforcement organizations within 10 minutes (or around 5 miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport, the Contracting Officer has determined the Lancaster Police Department (LPD) is the only source that can meet the specifications stated in the Statement of Work (SOW) to provide secure storage for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office SRT assets. There is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements as the rental of the secure storage facility described in the preceding paragraph is only available from the Town of Lancaster, and no other vendor offers services meeting these requirements. These services will be acquired through the use of FAR Part 12 procedures. Market Research conducted by OAQ and ERO determined there were no other providers of secure storage facilities with the level of security sufficient to meet agency requirements, and withing close proximity to the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport. OAQ and ERO have conducted extensive market research and used previous experience while attempting to identify other sources to meet mission requirements. Based on the market research conducted, there were no other available sources identified that would be able to provide a secure storage facility meeting the agency�s security requirements and proximity to Buffalo-Niagara International Airport. This notice of intent is NOT a request for proposals or quotes. Requests for copies of a solicitation in response to this notice will not be honored or acknowledged. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of whether conducting a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to fulfill this requirement by responding to this Notice of Intent no later than 9:00 AM Eastern Standard Time on September 10, 2026 by email to Andrew.Hadden@ice.dhs.gov; no telephone communications will be entertained. The subject line in the email shall state �Response to Notice of Intent � Rental of Secure Storage Facility Lancaster NY.� All information submitted should support the offeror�s capability to provide the supplies and services required and shall be furnished at no cost to the Government. The Government reserves the right to cancel the sole source award. The anticipated primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 493190 � Other Warehousing and Storage.

title: Long-Endurance, Fuel-Powered Maritime vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) Remotely Pilot Aerial Systems (RPAS)
description: The National Research Council of Canada's (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation, part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory, has a requirement for the supply of one (1) long-endurance, fuel-powered, single-rotor maritime vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS), High Eye Airboxer, including one (1) ground control station, a medium-range tracking antenna, an emergency flotation kit, an engine start kit, transport cases, integration and charging equipment, a maintenance package, a field repair kit, a simulator system and an AIS receiver, suitable for persistent operations from confined land-based and maritime environments and for the integration of specialized scientific, remote-sensing and surveillance payloads.

title: Siding and Window Replacement, Prince Edward Island National Park
description: 5P486-26-0137/A Siding and Window Replacement, Prince Edward Island National Park BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The objective of this project is the comprehensive removal of existing siding and the installation of a new vinyl siding system, including all associated trims and accessories on 2 (two) operational buildings in PEI National Park. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to complete the work in accordance with this Statement of Work. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $100,000 > $ 250,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than October 30, 2026. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT There will be a site visit on August 25, 2026 at 10:00 AM local time. Interested bidders are to meet at 40 Dalvay Crescent, York, PE, C0A 1P0 Safety Attire: In order to be guaranteed access to the site visit all persons should have the proper personal protection equipment (safety glasses, footwear, vests and hard hats etc.). Contractor’s personnel/individuals who do not have the proper safety attire may be denied access to the site. Bidders are requested to communicate with the Contracting Authority at least 24 hours before the optional site visit to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders may be requested to sign an attendance sheet. Bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative will not be given an alternative appointment but they will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than 5 business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

description: Canada is seeking offers from Offerors who are able to provide services for the conduct of chemical analysis for pesticide residues on crop samples collected from field trials at several Canadian and U.S. locations, in accordance with the requirements of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Principles of Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) (rev 1997), study plans and amendments and Health Canada’s Pesticides Regulatory Directorate “Residue Chemistry Guidelines” (PMRA Guidance Document, Updated Residue Chemistry Guidelines - Canada.ca). The data generated by these trials will be used in regulatory submissions to Health Canada’s Pesticides Regulatory Directorate (PRD) for new minor uses of pesticides.

Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/minerva-initiative-uncrewed-ground-system-surveillance-and-reconnaissance?auHash=l-oHqeoTmQmnsxQEUYMY5EaGpYMsj3ef1DLDTsG-TTY MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Ground System for Surveillance and Reconnaissance The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) requires an uncrewed ground system (UGS) to conduct ground surveillance and reconnaissance (S&R) that is domestically produced, easy to operate and maintain, and adequately rugged to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. MINERVA Initiative – Uncrewed Ground System for Surveillance and Reconnaissance Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 13, 2026 Closing date: September 10, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The Canadian Army (CA) soldier is facing an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the proliferation of multi-spectral sensors and precision weapons that will limit the CA’s ability to conduct surveillance and reconnaissance (S&R) operations and strike enemy targets at range by using attributable ballistic trajectory weapons without the risk of being targeted and attacked. The CA presently lacks an uncrewed ground system (UGS) capable of conducting ground-based surveillance and reconnaissance. The CA requires an innovative UGS that provides an uncrewed alternative to conduct persistent surveillance and route, area, and point reconnaissance tasks. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable, providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be composed of a : a. Ground Vehicle: The vehicle containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor Payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground Control Station (GCS): The system used by the human operator to control the vehicle and manage missions. Example of GCS components includes without limitation, laptop, tablet, handheld controller, etc. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UGS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/ data. e. Battery with Charger: A battery for the UGS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in a temperature range of -20°C and +40°C. 3. Weigh no more than 410kg in an unladen state. 4. Have a minimum operational radius of 3km (unladen) from the GCS while maintaining user control and live video via Radio Frequency link. 5. Operate at a minimum speed of 15km/hr and have a minimum endurance of 4hrs in continuous motion while in an unladen state. 6. Be capable of navigating paved roads, sand trails, and gravel trails during both day and night at a minimum gradient of 15 degrees (approach and lateral). 7. Have front-facing and rear-facing sensors that enable the operator to recognize¹ a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day – Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night – Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 0.5km 8. Be able to look over a minimum 1m obstacle and employ a pan or swivel capability to achieve a minimum of 180-degree field of vision. 9. Have sustained mobility of =7 km/h across while carrying its rated payload across roads, trails, and cross-country terrain. The vehicle must ascend 20% grades, traverse 15% side slopes, negotiate a 250 mm vertical step, and cross a 500 mm trench” ¹. “Recognize” is defined by the Johnson Criteria: Detection, Recognition, and Identification (DRI) are all guidelines that have been set in place by The Night Vision Thermal Imaging Systems Performance Model, also referred to as the Johnson criteria. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson%27s_criteria Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to a ready state in 30 minutes or less. This includes completing all tasks (i.e. unstrapping/unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set) such that the vehicle is fully prepped and ready to leave the line of departure. 2. Be sized such that a minimum of 2 UGS can be stowed for transport on a standard palletized loading system (PLS) deck (8 feet wide by 20 feet long). 3. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means that enables the operator to be a minimum of 100m away from the vehicle. 4. Be powered by electric or hybrid engines. 5. Incorporate front automated obstacle avoidance features. 6. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the vehicle. 7. Be transportable by a palletized loading system (PLS). 8. Be recoverable by a NATO-standard tow hook. 9. Have a minimum endurance of 48hrs while stationary and using its sensor payload. 10. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $150,000 CAD or less per system. 11. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UGS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: i. Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); ii. Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); iii. Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; iv. Real-time full motion video feed; and v. Battery life. e. title: Germany – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Rahmenvertrag externe Revisionsleistungen
description: Die Interne Revision der STADT UND LAND soll bei der Umsetzung des Jahresprüfungsplans fach-lich und personell durch einen externen Dienstleister unterstützt werden. Zu diesem Zweck ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrages vorgesehen, auf dessen Grundlage der Auftragnehmer die von der STADT UND LAND festgelegten Revisionsthemen bearbeitet. Die Prüfungsleistungen sind dabei im Co-Sourcing-Verfahren in enger Abstimmung mit der Internen Revision der STADT UND LAND zu erbringen. Die Prüfungen können insbesondere kaufmännische, immobilienwirtschaftliche, informationstechnologische sowie Governance-, Risiko- und Compliance-Prozesse des Konzerns betreffen. Hierzu zählen insbesondere Geschäfts-, Unterstützungs-, Steuerungs- und Überwachungsprozesse. Nicht Gegenstand dieses Rahmenvertrages sind bautechnische Prüfungen, Bauprojektprüfungen sowie sonstige Leistungen der Baurevision. Der Regelbedarf umfasst jährlich ein bis zwei Revisionsprüfungen. Darüber hinaus kann sich insbe-sondere aufgrund personeller Kapazitätsengpässe oder sonstiger betrieblicher Erfordernisse ein zusätzlicher Prüfungsbedarf ergeben. Da Umfang und Zeitpunkt eines solchen Mehrbedarfs im Vo-raus nicht verlässlich prognostiziert werden können, geht der Auftraggeber von bis zu neun Revisionsprüfungen pro Kalenderjahr aus. Ein Anspruch des Auftragnehmers auf Abruf eines bestimmten Leistungsumfangs besteht nicht.

title: Ireland – Construction work – Finglas Primary Care Centre
description: New build, four-storey with roof plant level, gross internal area approximately 10,517 sqm. The development comprises a HSE Primary Care Centre and GP block with a Tusla child and family agency office in the north-east block, served by two internal landscaped courtyards. The main public entrance is located on the south elevation off a new access road, with a secondary 7-day access entrance on the west elevation off Cardiffsbridge Road. The building is constructed over five levels with finished floor levels rising from 61.000m at Level 00 to 76.800m at Level 04, with roof plant set back 3.5m from the facade and screened at Level 04. External works include a connection to the new access road, 88 car parking spaces, 64 sheltered cycle spaces, hard and soft landscaping and all associated site and enabling works.

title: Germany – Engineering services – Ingenieurleistung zur Planung zum BV Neubau Kläranlage Klöden
description: Der Wasser- und Abwasserzweckverband "Elbe-Elster-Jessen" beabsichtigt die Kläranlage im Ortsteil Klöden neu zu bauen. Die Kläranlage befindet sich am Rande des Ortsteils Klöden (Stadt Jessen) im Landkreis Wittenberg in Sachsen-Anhalt. In Auswertung der vorhandenen Belastung wird die Kläranlage im Neukonzept nur noch auf eine Größe von 1.500 EW ausgelegt, da keine zusätzlichen Erschließungen in diesem Bereich geplant sind. Da sowohl das Belebungsbecken als auch das Nachklärbecken nicht sanierungswürdig sind, soll die biologische Reinigung komplett neu errichtet werden. Ebenfalls soll ein neuer Schlammstapelbehälter sowie ein neues Ablaufpumpwerk konzeptionell berücksichtigt werden. Der Neubau soll auf dem vorhandenen und bereits genutzten Grundstück des WAZV "Elbe-Elster-Jessen" erfolgen. Beim Bau der neuen Kläranlage muss der Weiterbetrieb der alten Kläranlage gewährleistet sein. Leistungsumfang: - Planungsleistungen gemäß Leistungsbild Ingenieurbauwerke § 43 HOAI 2021 Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 - 9 - Planungsleistungen gemäß Leistungsbild Technische Ausrüstung § 55 HOAI 2021 Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 - 9 - Planungsleistungen gemäß Leistungsbild Tragwerksplanung § 51 HOAI 2021 Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 - 6 - Planungsleistungen gemäß Leistungsbild Freianlagen § 39 HOAI 2021 Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 - 9 - Planungsleistungen gemäß Leistungsbild Verkehrsanlagen § 47 HOAI 2021 Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 1 - 9 - inklusive örtlicher Bauüberwachung

title: Growth Direct System Consumables
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) on behalf of the Center for Enabling Capabilities' (CEC) Pilot Bioproduction Facility (PBF) at the Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price contract on a sole source basis to Rapid Micro Biosystems, INC. 1001 Pawtucket Blvd West Suite 280, Lowell, MA USA; Cage Code 4TRL9 under the RFO FAR 6.103-1 � Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Description of Requirement: This is a requirement to establish a single award Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract vehicle that will allow the Center for Enabling Capabilities' (CEC) Pilot Bioproduction Facility (PBF) to procure the proprietary consumables required for the Government-owned Growth Direct� System currently used by the PBF. These consumables are manufactured by Rapid Micro Biosystems, Inc. and include Environmental Monitoring Cassettes (Part: ET80-100) and Environmental Monitoring Vision Lids (Part:EMVL-100), as well as freight associated with delivering the consumables. The Government will request Delivery Orders (DOs) be issued against this IDIQ on an as needed basis throughout the five-year IDIQ ordering period to deliver the needed consumables that are designed to enhance system performance. Approximately four DOs are anticipated per year throughout the five-year IDIQ ordering period. This special notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for this requirement. Meaningful submissions received in response to this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether a competitive procurement is in the best interest of the Government. If no meaningful, written submissions are received by the date listed below, after the publication of this notice, the solicitation will be issued as a sole source requirement to Rapid Micro Biosystems, INC. Based on the above information, the only technically acceptable vendor to fulfill this requirement is Rapid Micro Biosystems, INC. Submit capability statements (using PDF, MS Word, or Excel attachments) to Ms. Nicole Applegate at e-mail: nicole.v.applegate.civ@health.mil Capability statements are due no later than 10:00am Eastern Time on September 10, 2026.

title: Consulting Flood Hydrologist Services for the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
description: The agency seeks flood hydrologist consulting services for the purpose of performing in-depth reviewing/performing: � Watershed hydrologic modeling and associated uncertainties; � Probabilistic methods in estimating hydrologic hazard curves, including stochastic event flood modeling methods; � Site Specific, Statewide/Regional and Hydrometeorological Reports (HMRs) based Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP) and Probable Maximum Flood (PMF) analyses; � Regional frequency analysis to derive Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) of the precipitation and flood; � Climate change impact analyses on extreme precipitation using Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP) data and/or NASA Earth Exchange Global Daily Downscaled Projections; and � Other flood hydrology-related analyses for dam safety. Typical work efforts associated with the effort include but are not limited to: � Review of submitted analyses, including digital files, prepared by Licensees or their consultants. � Review of published data or reports from federal, state and local sources. � Attendance at Board of Consultants meetings and project meetings. � Provide expert advice to FERC staff on complex flood hydrology issues. � Review proposed scopes of work developed by Licensees or their consultants for consistency with the FERC guidelines and state-of-the-practice procedures. � Preparation of written reports as directed, with critiques, conclusions and recommendations. � Review and comment on correspondence or other communications to Licensees prepared by FERC staff. � Develop technical whitepapers to assist dam safety staff in reviewing/resolving complex technical topics � Provide technical topic training to FERC staff

description: Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Notice for information and planning purposes for qualified and experienced sources to provide Small Arms Weapons Instruction Support Services in support of Navy Expeditionary Combat Command (NECC) as defined in the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. It is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the Government for any purpose other than to gain the information requested, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. Interested parties are encouraged to respond to this RFI/Sources Sought Notice. Scope NECC requires qualified personnel with subject-matter expertise in small-arms weapons instruction, combat shooting techniques, and NECC training evolutions to perform the requirements of this attached PWS. A DRAFT performance work statement is provided containing further details (see Attachment I). title: DHS - FLETC - GLYNCO - FENCE UPGRADE
description: SITE VISIT 9/1/2026 - SEE ATTACHMENTS FLETC is required to adhere to Executive Order 14111 and the Interagency Security Committee (ISC) requirements for the physical security of federal facilities, which mandate robust perimeter protection in accordance with established standards. The currently installed perimeter security fence is non-compliant with anti-climb, anti-scale, and anti-crash ratings, creating a significant security vulnerability for the campus and its occupants. To address this risk and ensure compliance with ISC guidelines, the FLETC Chief Security Office (CSO) proposes the upgrade and replacement of the existing fencing with an approved perimeter fence designed and constructed in accordance with ISC, DHS, and FLETC physical security requirements, and in accordance with ASTM F2656 M30/P1, which specifies the impact resistance required to mitigate vehicle-borne threats. Implementing a perimeter fence will provide continuous, passive protection, eliminate the operational vulnerabilities associated with active barriers, and align the facility with current federal security standards.

description: 1. GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS A. Points of Contact (POCs) The points of contact for this solicitation are the Contracting Specialist and the Contracting Officer (KO). All questions and communications shall be submitted via email to the individuals listed below. Contracting Specialist Spenser Gagnon spenser.e.gagnon.civ@socom.mil Contracting Officer Samuel Williams samuel.williams1@socom.mil B. Mandatory Site Visit A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 24 August 2026 at 0900 EST. The purpose of this site visit is to allow prospective vendors the opportunity to inspect the physical spaces ask technical questions. C. Attendance and Eligibility for Award Attendance at this site visit is strict and mandatory for any prime contractor intending to submit a proposal. Representatives from the prime contractor must be physically present and must sign the official Government attendance roster at the start of the site visit. Proposals will only be accepted from vendors who attend the site visit and sign the roster. Proposals received from vendors who fail to attend will be deemed non-responsive and will be rejected without evaluation. No exceptions or waivers to this requirement will be granted. D. Registration and Base Access Requirements Vendors must notify the government points of contact listed in this solicitation of their intent to attend no later than 20 August 2026 at 12:00 PM EST. Along with the RSVP, vendors must submit required base access documentation, consisting of Names, Dates of Birth, and Driver's License Numbers on company letterhead, to the listed points of contact by the RSVP deadline. It is the sole responsibility of the vendor to ensure they can gain physical access to Camp Lejeune and the MARFORSOC Compound. Access to the MARFORSOC Compound is a separate security process, and general access to Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune does not guarantee or grant entry to the MARFORSOC Compound. The Government is not responsible for any vendor's failure to gain base entry in time for the site visit. E. Proposal Submission Proposals shall be received no later than 10:00 AM EST on 10 September 2026. Proposals shall be submitted electronically via email to the POCs listed above. Hard copy or physical media submissions shall not be accepted. F. Commercial Acquisition Notice Offerors are advised that this is a commercial acquisition conducted utilizing simplified procedures under FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). The Government will utilize a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) evaluation process as detailed in Section M. G. Proposal Organization Offerors shall submit a clear, concise proposal that demonstrates a thorough understanding of the requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW). Proposals shall be structured into three distinct volumes as outlined below. Volume Title Page Limit Volume I Technical Capability (Acceptable/Unacceptable Gates) 15 Pages (resumes and certifications do not count) Volume II Past Performance 5 Pages Volume III Price & Contract Documentation No Page Limit H. Contract Type and Structure The Government intends to award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) commercial purchase order. The contract shall consist of a Base Year and four (4) Option Years for recurring semi-annual preventative maintenance and replacement parts. I. Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) Applicability Statutory Mandate: Offerors are notified that this procurement is subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. Chapter 67), formerly known as the Service Contract Act (SCA). Wage Determination: Any contract resulting from this solicitation will incorporate U.S. Department of Labor Wage Determination No. 2015-4389 (Revision 34, dated 7/30/2026) for Onslow County, North Carolina, which is attached to this solicitation under Section J. Price Adjustments: Pursuant to FAR 52.222-43 (Fair Labor Standards Act and Service Contract Labor Standards--Price Adjustment (Multiple Year and Option Contracts)), the contractor may warrant price adjustments in option years only to the extent that wage rates are increased by the Department of Labor through subsequent revisions to the wage determination. 2. VOLUME INSTRUCTIONS VOLUME I - TECHNICAL CAPABILITY The Technical Volume shall contain the objective documentation required to prove the offeror meets the Government's minimum standards. No pricing or labor rate information shall be included in this volume. Sub-Factor 1: Mandatory Site Visit Verification The Offeror shall explicitly state in their proposal the name(s) of the company representative(s) who physically attended the mandatory site visit on 24 August 2026 and signed the official Government attendance roster. Sub-Factor 2: OEM Partner/Reseller Certification The Offeror shall demonstrate their capability to support the proprietary high-security architecture of the MARSOC CCTV network by providing active, verifiable manufacturer documentation of the following: Genetec Authorized Partner/Reseller Status: Proof that the prime contractor is certified to sell, install, integrate, and support Genetec Streamvault Workstations and Genetec Network Video Recorders (NVRs) as listed in SOW Section 5.3. Axis Communications Certified Partner Status: Proof that the prime contractor is an authorized partner/reseller certified to support the Axis IP cameras deployed across the barracks. Sub-Factor 3: Key Personnel Qualifications & Clearances The Offeror shall submit resumes and professional certifications for the following three (3) core roles required for contract performance: Project Manager: Must possess a minimum of three (3) years of experience managing physical security or CCTV system installation/maintenance contracts. Lead AV Programmer/Systems Engineer: Must hold active Crestron Certified Master Programmer and Cisco CCNA (or higher) certifications to program and manage the workstation interfaces and Cisco network switches listed in the SOW. Lead AV Technician: Must possess a minimum of three (3) years of experience installing and troubleshooting IP-based CCTV cameras. Security Clearance Mandate: The Offeror shall provide explicit written certification that all three proposed key personnel possess active SECRET security clearances at the time of proposal submission, in accordance with the DD Form 254. Sub-Factor 4: Preventative Maintenance & Emergency Response Plan The Offeror shall submit a streamlined, non-technical execution plan (not to exceed 3 pages) demonstrating their operational capability to meet the following SOW-mandated response windows: Semi-Annual Inspections: A plan to execute the test and inspection of all system components, battery backup systems, and UPS units twice per year with at least six months between visits. Emergency Repair Response: A plan confirming the capability to respond to emergency repair requests within twenty-four (24) hours of notification on typical business days (M-F), to include diagnosing cabling issues supporting the CCTV system. VOLUME II - PAST PERFORMANCE The Offeror shall submit a maximum of three (3) past performance references demonstrating recent and relevant experience. Recency: Efforts must have been performed within the last three (3) years from the issuance date of this solicitation. Relevance: Efforts must involve the installation, maintenance, or repair of IP-based CCTV networks, physical security systems, or network-video recording infrastructure of similar scope (preferably within a DoD environment, military installation, or secure government facility). Reference Details: For each reference, the Offeror shall provide: Contract Number or Purchase Order Number. Customer Agency/Unit and Point of Contact (Name, Email, and Phone Number of the CO or COR). Total Contract Value. Period of Performance. A brief narrative describing the services performed. title: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source: Globus High Assurance Subscription Renewal
description: GENERAL This notice is issued in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 12.201-1(c)(2), advertising the Government's intent to issue an award on a sole source basis under the authority established in RFO 12.102(a). The National Institutes of Health, Specialized Scientific Information Technology (SSIT) Division anticipates issuing a single Purchase Order (PO) to the following entity: The University of Chicago 401 N. Michigan Avenue, Suite 900 Chicago, IL 60611 BACKGROUND The intramural NIH campus utilizes Globus function as a service (FaaS) within the High-Performance Computation Biowulf Cluster as a centralized service for the NIH scientific community. Many NICHD scientists in the intramural NICHD community routinely transfer data to and from Helix/Biowulf and other major computational centers on campus, and it is vital for them to have appropriate, secure, and user-friendly tools such as Globus. Globus at the University of Chicago is proprietary software and the only commercially available product that can properly maintain all the essential functionalities required in support of the intramural scientists need to transfer data to and from Helix/Biowulf. Globus utilizes a secure endoint to endpoint transfer system specifically developed for transferring high-performance research data - allowing the NICHD to transfer data exceeding several terabytes in size. Globus maintains transfer status in the event of network outages, minimizing negative impacts to transfer operations and research timelines. There is no other compatible software that can properly and adequately support the Government with this need. Market research indicates that Globus is the proprietary vendor and therefore, is a sole source. RESPONSES There will not be a solicitation or competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) issued as a result of this announcement. Any responses or inquiries to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition will be advantageous to the Government. Notwithstanding the stated intent, if other organizations believe they can fully meet the Government�s requirement, they must submit written documentation of their capabilities. The capabilities statement must contain sufficient documentation to establish a bona fide capability to fulfill the requirement and must be received by the response date listed in this posting. A general statement which merely states the entity is capable will not be sufficient. A determination not to compete with this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. NIH will not be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties in responding to this notice. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the evaluation of the information received. Interested parties may respond and provide a capability statement no later than the date specified in this notice. Emails must reference the announcement number in the subject line. This is not an RFQ, and this announcement does not commit the Government to award a contract.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for NMR Gaussmeter
description: Notice of Intent to Noncompetitively acquire a Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Gaussmeter This notice is not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued, and quotations will not be requested. This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of RFO 12.102(a). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 334516, Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing which has a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Physical Measurement Laboratory (PML), Nanoscale Device Characterization Division, Advanced Electronics Group intends to purchase a gaussmeter whose operating principle is the nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) of protons. Additionally, the gaussmeter must be calibrated and traceable to international standards. A primary strategic focus of the division involves exploring the chemical and physical nature of atomic-scale defects in materials. Chief among these materials is diamond; including applications exploiting its wide bandgap properties for power electronics and its ultra-stable defect entities for use in quantum sensing applications. The division is currently undertaking an effort to develop diamond-based magnetometers for magnetic field sensing. A critical aspect of this program is the precise measure of the electronic g-tensor of a specific diamond-based defect entity, the nitrogen vacancy (NV) center. Our ability to measure this quantity directly relates to our ability to calibrate the magnetic field of our magnets. Thus, we require an ultra-sensitive NMR gaussmeter. Additionally, our program requires that our measure of g-tensor be SI traceable and thus requires an SI-traceable measure of magnetic field. The primary purpose of this acquisition is to measure magnetic field in an ultra-sensitive and SI-traceable manner by exploiting the nuclear magnetic resonance of protons. This unit will serve to measure and verify against international standards the magnetic fields of our existing magnet infrastructure. The ability to perform this is ultimately directly related to the sensitivity and traceability of the diamond-based magnetometers currently under development. In order to realize this mission, NIST requires an NMR Gaussmeter that meets all essential minimum technical specifications identified below: The gaussmeter shall operate on the principle of nuclear magnetic resonance of protons. The gaussmeter shall be a standalone instrument that does not require integration or requirements of any other systems. The gaussmeter shall have a precision of less than 0.01 parts per million in a stable magnetic field of 1.5 T. The gaussmeter shall have an accuracy of plus or minus 5 parts per million that is independent of temperature. The gaussmeter shall have a maximum field gradient of at least 1 mT per cm. The gaussmeter shall have an operating frequency range covering at least 1 MHz to 1 GHz. The gaussmeter shall have the ability to accept interchangeable probe heads for measuring a variety of different magnetic field ranges. The gaussmeter shall come furnished with one such probe head that shall Cover the magnetic field range of 200 mT through 500 mT. Include a remote passive measurement head in which the electronic components are separated from the active measurement area of the probe. Be sized such that the remote passive measurement area of the probe will fit into a space 1.5 mm x 9.5 mm. The gaussmeter shall be calibrated and must Be traceable to standards maintained in accordance with international agreements and the SI system of units. Include a calibration certificate stating The instrument, serial number and date of calibration. The entity performing the calibration. Standards utilized. Measurement methods. Measurement results that include uncertainty. NIST conducted market research from May to August 2026 to determine what sources could potentially meet NIST�s minimum requirements. This included searches on Google, GSA; SAM; surveying vendor websites; and issuance of a Sources Sought Notice on SAM.gov. Market research identified various manufacturers of NMR Gaussmeters, but only one can provide a commercial product that meets all of the above listed essential specifications. The results of market research revealed that only Metrolabs Technologies SA provides an NMR Gaussmeter that meets all required specifications (NMR Precision Teslameter PT2026), and GMW Associates is their sole, exclusive reseller of this product in the United States. Therefore, GMW Associates (UEI: D69RTQNNVGP4) appears to be capable of meeting NIST�s requirements. However, any sources that believe they are capable of meeting NIST�s minimum requirements are encouraged to respond to this notice by the response date to provide the following information at a minimum: Company Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number in https://sam.gov; details about what your company is capable of providing that meets or exceeds NIST�s minimum requirements; whether your company is an authorized reseller of the product or service being cited and evidence of such authorization; and any other information that can help NIST determine whether this requirement may be competitively satisfied. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Only responses received by the offers due date and time of this notice will be considered by the government. Responses shall be submitted via email to the primary point of contact indicated in this notice.

title: DHS - FLETC - GLYNCO - FENCE UPGRADE
description: SITE VISIT ATTENDEES SHEET ADDED TO ATTACHMENTS AMENDMENT ONE - update RFQ, adds 2 attachments, clarifies items SITE VISIT 9/1/2026 - SEE ATTACHMENTS FLETC is required to adhere to Executive Order 14111 and the Interagency Security Committee (ISC) requirements for the physical security of federal facilities, which mandate robust perimeter protection in accordance with established standards. The currently installed perimeter security fence is non-compliant with anti-climb, anti-scale, and anti-crash ratings, creating a significant security vulnerability for the campus and its occupants. To address this risk and ensure compliance with ISC guidelines, the FLETC Chief Security Office (CSO) proposes the upgrade and replacement of the existing fencing with an approved perimeter fence designed and constructed in accordance with ISC, DHS, and FLETC physical security requirements, and in accordance with ASTM F2656 M30/P1, which specifies the impact resistance required to mitigate vehicle-borne threats. Implementing a perimeter fence will provide continuous, passive protection, eliminate the operational vulnerabilities associated with active barriers, and align the facility with current federal security standards.
